comparisons.coverage_method: Verified the complete 135-entry manifest against the selectors `libero/libero/bddl_files/*.bddl`, `libero/libero/benchmark/*.py`, and `libero/libero/envs/predicates/*.py` at commit 8f1084e3132a39270c3a13ebe37270a43ece2a01. Reviewed the full definition inventory for pouring, screening, straining, sorting, agitation, receptacle transfer, and release goals, and read the closest original BDDL definition in full. No selector or registry coverage gap was found.
comparisons.objective: The candidate pours a mixed batch into a supported apertured screen, physically separates ceramic finishing media from retained metal washers, clears bridges by controlled screen motion, and releases the screen onto supports. LIBERO's closest task transfers one cream-cheese object into a bowl.
comparisons.physical_skill: The candidate tests bulk pouring followed by size-and-orientation-dependent passage, bimanual load sharing, controlled agitation, spill prevention, selective retention, and stable tool release. LIBERO tests ordinary single-object pickup and receptacle placement without granular flow or physical separation.
comparisons.success_condition: The candidate measures admitted mixture mass and recovered media mass, requires at least 98% media recovery with every washer retained, and invalidates spill, contamination, loss, or damage before a released three-second dwell. LIBERO requires only an `On` relation between one object and a bowl.

closest_tasks.name: put_the_cream_cheese_in_the_bowl
closest_tasks.objective: Put one cream-cheese object in or on a bowl.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Single rigid-object grasp, transport, and receptacle placement.
closest_tasks.success_condition: The cream-cheese object satisfies `On cream_cheese_1 akita_black_bowl_1`.
closest_tasks.reason: This is the closest receptacle-transfer goal, but it has no mixed bulk contents, apertured tool, selective passage, bridging, agitation, retained workpieces, or recovery-efficiency criterion.

comparisons.reason: Across the complete LIBERO registry, constituent placement skills exist, but no task tests physical screening of a mixed batch through orientation-dependent apertures while retaining a second object class.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified all 381 manifest entries against `robocasa/environments/kitchen/*.py`, `robocasa/environments/__init__.py`, and `robocasa/utils/dataset_registry.py` at commit 425684d332f135f5b30a40b321f52d15a0fe9250. Reviewed the complete class/docstring inventory for pouring, draining, straining, sorting, shaking, receptacle transfer, and tool placement, then read the complete implementations of the strongest motion-level and transfer-level neighbors.
comparisons.objective: The candidate uses a manual screen to recover small finishing media from a washer/media mixture while retaining every washer. RoboCasa's nearest tasks shake a pan containing one vegetable or dump a vegetable from a pot into a sink, wash it, and return it.
comparisons.physical_skill: ShakePan overlaps in grasping, lifting, agitating a loaded vessel, keeping its contents contained, and returning the vessel to a support. DrainVeggies overlaps in dumping contents between receptacles. Neither task uses true apertures to produce a size-and-orientation-selective split, clears granular bridges, or coordinates two arms around a large loaded screen.
comparisons.success_condition: The candidate grades mass recovery and exact washer retention, forbids any escaped media or receiver contamination, and requires released support dwell. ShakePan succeeds after accumulated vessel movement with the vegetable still in the pan and the pan back on the stove; DrainVeggies succeeds after a single vegetable is washed and returned to its pot.

closest_tasks.name: ShakePan
closest_tasks.objective: Grip and lift a pan, shake a vegetable inside it, and put the pan back on the stove.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Loaded-vessel grasping, agitation while retaining contents, replacement on a support, and release.
closest_tasks.success_condition: After at least 25 qualifying movement updates, the vegetable remains in the pan and the pan is on the correct stove location.
closest_tasks.reason: It is the closest dynamic-tool task, but its scorer rewards generic pan displacement rather than physical passage, bridge clearing, or separation of two intermixed object populations.

closest_tasks.reason: It includes dumping and recovery but does not drain through a perforated implement or separate mixed constituents by geometry.

comparisons.reason: RoboCasa supplies meaningful agitation and content-transfer neighbors, but none tests aperture-mediated granular separation with selective retention and quantified recovery.

comparisons.objective: The candidate pours and screens a two-component bulk mixture, recovers the media, retains all washers, and replaces the screen. SimplerEnv's closest environment puts one source object on or in one target.

comparisons.success_condition: The candidate requires quantitative media recovery, zero washer loss, no spill or contamination, screen support, gripper clearance, and fresh dwell. PutOnInSceneEnv succeeds from a geometric/contact relation for one source and one target.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified the complete 1,122-file manifest against both repositories' activity-definition selectors plus the recorded BEHAVIOR task and predicate-mapping implementations at commits b544acbbb76b461349bcba21f93b870b11da6608 and 06bec10ca54c7f375a1f71da8b94f7e1896ff77a. Searched the complete activity inventory for sieves, screens, pouring, draining, sorting, mixtures, and granular transfer, then read the closest sieve and contents-transfer definitions in full. The sieve activity's actual goal is an abstract cleanliness state, not filtering.
comparisons.objective: The candidate physically separates ceramic media from washers with an apertured screen. BEHAVIOR includes cleaning a sieve and pouring water into a glass, but neither uses a sieve to divide a mixture.
comparisons.physical_skill: CleanASieve manipulates cleaning supplies to remove a covering state from a sieve, while PouringWaterInAGlass transfers one liquid category between containers. The candidate instead depends on rigid granular geometry: some bodies must pass end-first through apertures while washers remain, with controlled agitation to clear bridges without spill.
comparisons.success_condition: The candidate requires at least 98% recovered media, every washer retained, no loss or contamination, supported screen release, and a revocable dwell. CleanASieve only requires removal of `covered`; PouringWaterInAGlass requires a glass on a counter and `filled` with water.

closest_tasks.physical_skill: Cleaning a tool surface with water, soap, and a sponge.
closest_tasks.success_condition: The sieve is no longer in the `covered` state with respect to the adhesive material.
closest_tasks.reason: The shared sieve noun does not create ability overlap: its holes never filter a mixture, and the goal measures cleanliness rather than selective passage or recovery.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified both exact manifest files and the authoritative ten-task Tier-1 catalog. comparisons.objective: The candidate performs post-finishing bulk separation and media recovery with a manual screen. DataCenterBench contains switches, covers, a keypad, connectors, a slider, and cable routing; its nearest task is a bimanual connector join.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both tasks require coordinated use of two arms and controlled contact. DC-join stabilizes a coupler while aligning and inserting one plug. The candidate instead shares a loaded screen between two grippers, agitates many free bodies through apertures, prevents spill, retains washers, and reseats the tool.
comparisons.success_condition: The candidate uses fractional mass recovery, exact retention, damage/loss disqualifiers, and released dwell. DC-join is binary and succeeds when a plug is fully inserted with no gap.

closest_tasks.success_condition: The Ethernet plug is fully inserted into the coupler with no gap.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified all 110 manifest entries against every `task/RoboDojo/tasks/*.py`, `task/RoboDojo/config/*.yml`, and `task/RoboDojo/task_registry.py` file at commit fbfbbcb3801397fa00dcffaef3ca64d97c3fe76f. Reviewed the complete task/config inventory for pouring, sorting, shaking, containers, granular objects, and release, then read the complete Python and YAML originals for the closest multi-object pouring task.
comparisons.objective: The candidate pours a washer/media mixture into a screen and uses aperture-selective motion to recover media while retaining washers. RoboDojo's nearest task pours seven balls from a cup into a vase.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both require controlling a loaded container, pouring multiple free rigid bodies through an opening, avoiding misses or mouth jams, restoring the tool upright, and releasing it. The candidate adds a second object class that must remain in the screen, bimanual manipulation of a large apertured tool, orientation-dependent passage, deliberate bridge clearing, and mass-based recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: The candidate gives partial credit for admitted mixture and recovered media, requires 98% recovery and complete washer retention, and permanently penalizes spill, contamination, and damage. PourBallsIntoVase is all-or-nothing: all seven balls must be inside the vase, the cup upright, and the robot back at origin.

closest_tasks.name: pour_balls_into_vase
closest_tasks.quote: Pour all the balls from the cup into the vase.
closest_tasks.objective: Pour seven balls from a cup into a vase, then restore and release the cup.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Multi-body rigid pouring through a restricted opening, avoidance of misses or mouth jams, and tool replacement.
closest_tasks.success_condition: All seven spheres are inside the vase, the cup is upright, and the robot has returned to origin.
closest_tasks.reason: This is a substantive overlap in controlled multi-body pouring, but its tested endpoint is complete transfer of one homogeneous population; it does not test physical classification by apertures, simultaneous retention of washers, screen agitation, or recovery yield.

comparisons.reason: RoboDojo contains a real granular-pouring neighbor, but the candidate's central tested ability is selective physical separation of two intermixed populations rather than transferring every particle to one receptacle.
